what_matters.head: 32 of the 35 names fell, and the chip fund lost 8.3%, about 2.0 × its usual day; the S&P 500 fund fell only 0.5%
what_matters.detail: Each name is counted at its latest session: New York and Europe on Tuesday, Seoul and Singapore part-way through Wednesday. Reuters says the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 closed lower as Nvidia and other AI-related shares gave back some of Monday's sharp gains and investors braced for possible new tariffs. Technology was the weakest S&P 500 sector, down 2.8%, an index of chip stocks fell 7.9% and the Dow rose 0.85% (Reuters). Yahoo Finance says chip stocks declined with the rest of the AI trade as worries about a December rate rise returned to focus; the 10-year yield fell 1bp on the day. On the tariffs, Reuters, citing three unnamed people, says the US Trade Representative is about to release the findings of its Section 301 probe into excess industrial capacity in 16 trading partners, among them China, Taiwan, South Korea, Singapore and the European Union, and that new import duties on a wide range of goods are expected. The report gives no rates and does not mention chips. AP, citing two unnamed people, said on Wednesday that the findings are expected in the coming days. Nvidia fell 5.9%; Reuters says investors refocused on the political and governance risks of Jensen Huang's return.

what_matters.head: Aixtron fell 16.3% in Frankfurt, about 3.3 × its usual day, after UBS cut it to 'sell'
what_matters.detail: UBS cut Aixtron to 'sell' from 'neutral' and its 12-month price target to €24 from €50, citing an expected slowdown in 2028 in demand for equipment used to make lasers for AI data-centre networking (Investing.com, which had the shares down 10% when it reported). Frankfurt closes about 4½ hours before New York. AXT fell 16.9% in New York, about 2.0 × its usual day and the largest percentage fall on the list; no reported cause was found for it.

what_matters.head: US GDP (Q3, second estimate) and October PCE inflation are due tonight at 21:30 SGT
what_matters.detail: The Bureau of Economic Analysis publishes both at 8:30 a.m. New York time. The first estimate of third-quarter growth was 3.4% at an annual rate. In September PCE prices rose 0.5% on the month and 3.6% on the year, and 0.3% and 3.1% excluding food and energy. The Fed next meets on 8-9 Dec; Reuters says futures put the odds of a rate rise in December at 97% (CME FedWatch). US markets are closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving and close early on Friday, at 13:00 New York time (02:00 SGT on Saturday).

after_data.text: Dell reported after Tuesday's close: revenue of $54.94B against the $49.32B analysts expected, and adjusted earnings per share of $9.45 against $6.59. It ended the quarter with a record $132.3B backlog of AI server orders after booking $60.2B of new ones, raised its full-year revenue forecast to $202B from $192B and approved another $25B of share buybacks. It expects the memory chip shortage to continue into 2027. Its AI servers run on Nvidia chips. The shares rose about 5% after hours (Reuters). None of this is in Tuesday's US prices.

after_data.lead: Asia and US futures on Wednesday
after_data.text: S&P 500 futures were down 0.7% and Nasdaq 100 futures 1.4% at 14:33 SGT (Investing.com). Taiwan's index closed down 4.8% after falling more than 8% earlier (Al Jazeera), and Japan's Nikkei fell 2.8% (AP, Al Jazeera). None of this is in Tuesday's US prices.

The rule that puts Megaspeed and six other firms in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand on the US Entity List was published in the Federal Register on Wednesday 25 Nov, effective 23 Nov. A licence is required to send them any item covered by US export rules, and applications are reviewed under a presumption of denial. Goods already on their way on 23 Nov may be delivered until 23 Dec.

after_data.lead: Trump on a US stake in Nvidia
after_data.text: President Trump told the New York Post he had thought about the US government taking an equity stake in Nvidia: 'I said, "You know, maybe I should do it," but I didn't bring it up at this point. It's probably not too late' (Reuters). He also said he is willing to pardon Jensen Huang if necessary. No step has been announced. The reports found do not make clear whether the remarks were public before Tuesday's close.

Reuters says Nvidia closed lower as Monday's rally lost steam, with investors refocusing on the political and governance risks of Jensen Huang's return. Huang told employees on Tuesday that he had violated some of the company's code of conduct (Reuters, citing one person familiar with the matter).

Investing.com's German report calls Infineon the DAX's biggest faller and puts it down to the reversal of Monday's technology rally and fears of new US import tariffs; it says there was no company news (read through search results).
Yahoo Finance says Micron gave back some of Monday's double-digit gain as the AI trade came under renewed pressure, and ties the chip sector's fall to worries about a December rate rise.

Reuters says Anthropic ended below its $83 IPO price and gives no reason. Yahoo Finance cites Needham analysts, who point to Anthropic's large capital needs, a credit rating it has not yet shared, possible selling by insiders and ordinary profit-taking after an IPO.

AP says Asian chip stocks fell on Wednesday after AI shares tumbled on Wall Street, with relief over Jensen Huang's return tempered by questions over Nvidia's governance; Investing.com also cites fresh US tariff threats.
